x: Ted Read won the 100 Yards, while Charlie Smart won the 3 Miles, and proved how sadly we missed him during the season while he was overseas with the B.A.O.R.

Jack Frost was second in the first 220 Yards, while Ted Read won the second-string race. Len Marchant found young Anzola, the T.V.H. lad, a little too speedy down the straight in the 880, but Len Herbert won the 1 Mile with D.
Bob Wise was second in the High Jump and Charlie Jones won the Long Jump, and we won the Medley Relay with Len Marchant, Jack Frost, Ted Read and Syd Jarlett.
The latter, however, won the 220 with Ted Read in second place. Morris, the Police champion, won the 880 Yards and Alf Orton ran well to credit us with third place.
Ted Read gave us an encouraging start by winning the 100 Yards in 10.4 secs, but could only manage third place in the 220, which was won by B.
The 100 Yards Club Championship was won by Ted Read, who beat Dicky Dumbrill with Jack Frost third, and the holder, Stan Botwright, beaten into fourth place.
Higgins, the Public Schools' quarter champion, beat Ted Read in the 220, and scored a double by also winning the 440, in which Jack Frost finished third.

Eventually six Senior and seven Juniors arrived at the ground, and Ted Read did well to gain second place in his heat of the 100 Yards. Syd Jarlett also ran second in his 440 heat, and then Charlie Jones gained third place in the Long Jump, which he followed up with second place in the Javelin.
Basil Walden won the final from Ted Read, the scratch man, and A.
Held at Charlton Park on July 30th, and again our numbers were very few, although Ted Read won the 100 and Bob Wise the 220.
Held at Tooting Track on August 2nd, before a large crowd, and some good racing was seen. Ted Read retained his 100 yards title, with a newcomer in G.

Held on the fine Police ground, this match took the form of a six-sided conest and in coming out on top our lads can be said to have done well. Ted Read scored a double in the two short sprints and Jim Beaumont managed a fourth place in the 440.
With Ted Read still in the R.A.F. we naturally cannot expect him to turn out on every occasion, but without him we do not seem to win many sprint events.
The Wandsworth team was captained by Dave Grigg, the English International, and in the 100 yards Ted Read was beaten by inches by Jackson of Herne Hill in 10.4 secs.

It was a neck-and-neck struggle between South London Harriers and ourselves throughout, and our members can be said to have done well against such opposition. Ted Read ran second to Liffen of S.L.H. in the 100, while Jack Frost was second in the first strings 220 yards, and E.

Ted Read was third in the Surrey 220 yards and Willie Nankeville was second with Len Marchant third in the 880 at the same meeting. Len Herbert finished third in a 4 min. 24.2 secs., 1 mile race, with Jimmy Wood, a second-claim member in second place.
Len Marchant was third in the 880 yards, won in 1 min. 57.4 secs., and Ted Read qualified for the second round in the 220 yards but could not progress further.

Ted Read and Les Christmas were first and second in the 220 yards, and we also won the medley relay race. Final scores saw us lose the match by the narrow margin of one point, we scored 46 to the home club's 47, with Worthing scoring 37.
